newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firm, foreigners buy on auction.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firm, foreigners buy on auction.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed slightly firmer on Tuesday as foreign investors bought pesos to invest in the money market ahead of the primary auction of Cetes, or T-bills.

"The market calmed down with a few dollars. We saw foreigners interested in peso investments thinking that medium-term rates could fall again," said Pablo Perrusquia, an analyst with the Inverlat financial group.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate both closed 0.1 of a centavo stronger at 7.8750/7.8800 and 7.8730/7.8740 per dollar, respectively.
A Reuters survey of money market traders revealed an average forecast of 27.66 percent for bellwether 28-day Cetes rates, which would be 142 basis points below last week's assignment rate.
The prospect of lower rates also attracted buying in the stock market. The leading IPC index of Mexican stocks was up 1.74 percent at 3,368.62 points as the foreign exchange market closed.

Traders said the session was generally calm, apart from a short-lived bout of speculative dollar buying prompted by Monday's sudden announcement that Antonio Lozano had been fired as Attorney General.

"The Lozano ousting only had an effect at the open, and then the market apparently took it in its stride. The outlook is favorable, interest rates and the bourse are developing favorably," said a trader.
Overnight rates on Cetes were down 40 basis points at 27.40 percent in late trade.
